[Thinking]
**Explaining virtualenv-delete**

When discussing `pyenv virtualenv-delete`, I need to clarify that it removes the entire virtual environment along with its packages. It's important to warn about active environments and suggest backing up. The command is `pyenv virtualenv-delete [-f] <name>`, and it deletes the directory under `/.pyenv/versions/<name>`. To see installed virtual environments, I can use `pyenv virtualenvs`. If necessary, I can mention exporting requirements with `pip freeze > requirements.txt` before deletion and advise the user to deactivate any active environment first.
[/Thinking]

Yes — pyenv virtualenv-delete removes the entire virtualenv directory, so all packages installed inside that virtualenv will be removed.

A few practical notes:
- It deletes the virtualenv found under ~/.pyenv/versions/<venv-name> (or wherever your PYENV_ROOT is), so everything in that environment goes with it.
- It will not touch other virtualenvs or your system/global Python/site-packages.
- If the environment is currently activated, deactivate it first (exit the shell or run deactivate) to avoid surprises.
- To avoid the confirmation prompt you can use the force flag (examples depend on your pyenv-virtualenv version): pyenv virtualenv-delete -f <venv-name>
- If you want to preserve a list of packages before deleting, run pip freeze > requirements.txt from inside the venv so you can recreate it later.

To list virtualenvs before deletion: pyenv virtualenvs
To delete: pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name> (or with -f to skip confirmation)
